messages.content: Can you help me find public libraries in New York, NY that have a Reading Room and Fiction section, and then in Los Angeles, CA that offer Wi-Fi and have a Children Section, and finally in Chicago, IL that have a Cafe and a Reading Room?

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. We need to call it three times with appropriate parameters.

The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: ...}) => any.

Facilities can be "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter expects a single value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." It lists options. But maybe we can pass an array? The type says "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". That seems ambiguous. It might accept a single string or an array of strings. We'll assume we can pass an array of strings.

Thus for New York, NY: Reading Room and Fiction section. So facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Los Angeles, CA: Wi-Fi and Children Section. So facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Chicago, IL: Cafe and Reading Room. So facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. We'll produce separate calls.
